header.title: Multipolar industrial landscape distributes leadership across US, Europe, Japan and China

s01_bottom_line.text: The article documents a more multipolar global industrial landscape: the US leading frontier tech/capital/demand, Europe in software/automation/equipment, Japan in precision, and China in scaled deployment and integrated supply chains.
The article frames China's role as evolving ('made by China') within a geographically dispersed, multipolar supply chain rather than retreating from trade.
This suggests region- and role-specific industrial exposures rather than a single winner, implying selection across geographies; the article names no specific companies.

items.text: In a multipolar industrial landscape Europe leads selected software/automation/equipment, Japan precision/efficiency, and China scaled deployment and integrated supply chains.
The U.S. leads in frontier technology, capital and demand, positioned to benefit from AI infrastructure, reshoring and electrification.
China is positioning itself as a provider of the technologies, equipment and industrial capabilities enabling manufacturing growth worldwide — 'made by China'.
